---
title: "Configure the preview"
description: "Tune rebuild behavior, popup appearance, Pandoc, and other preview options."
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

The defaults work well for most packages, so you can usually just run
`updoc::serve()`. When you want to tweak how rebuilds work or how the preview
looks, every option below works with both [`serve()`](../reference/serve.html)
and [`preview()`](../reference/preview.html).

## Rebuilding

Use `strategy` to choose how updoc responds when you save a file:

- `"smart"` *(default)*: rebuilds only the pages affected by your edit (a single
  article, changed reference pages, `NEWS.md`, or site CSS), and falls back to a
  full build for broader changes like `_pkgdown.yml`, `DESCRIPTION`, R code
  edits, or deleted files.
- `"lazy"`: runs pkgdown's lazy build, skipping reference pages and articles
  whose output is already newer than their source files.
- `"full"`: rebuilds the whole site on every save. Slower, but handy when
  debugging cross-page links or site-wide layout changes.

```r
updoc::serve(strategy = "full")
```

When you edit files in `R/`, updoc runs roxygen2 in its temporary preview copy
so reference pages stay current. If you maintain `man/` files yourself (or don't
use roxygen2), turn that off:

```r
updoc::serve(document = FALSE)
```

Even with `document = FALSE`, updoc still checks your R files for syntax errors
and renders `README.Rmd` if you edit it.

## Pandoc

updoc uses whichever Pandoc installation rmarkdown finds (2.10.1 or newer). To
point it at another copy, pass the folder containing the `pandoc` binary (not
the binary itself):

```r
updoc::serve(pandoc = "/path/to/pandoc/bin")
```

To make that your default for `serve()`, `preview()`, and `build()`, add it to
your session or `.Rprofile`:

```r
options(updoc.pandoc = "/path/to/pandoc/bin")
```

Passing `pandoc` directly always overrides the option. updoc never downloads
Pandoc automatically or changes your system installation.

## Build output and logs

Full, unfiltered output from your latest build is always saved to a temporary
log file (even when `quiet = TRUE`), and stays available for the rest of your R
session:

- After `site <- updoc::preview()`, find the file at `site$status()$build_log`.
- After `result <- updoc::build()`, find it at `result$build_log` (or on the
  error object's `$build_log` if the build failed).

To keep your console clean, updoc hides two harmless Pandoc 3.11 deprecation
warnings (`--mathml` and `--mathjax`) from normal output while still writing
them to the log. All other warnings and errors appear as usual.

## Popup appearance

Use `theme` to control how the in-browser status popup looks:

| Value | Appearance |
| --- | --- |
| `"auto"` | Matches the site's light or dark theme, falling back to your system preference |
| `"inverse"` | The opposite of `"auto"` (dark popup on a light site, light on dark) |
| `"light"` | Always light |
| `"dark"` | Always dark |

Set it for a single session with `updoc::serve(theme = "dark")`, or set a
personal default in your `.Rprofile`:

```r
options(updoc.theme = "inverse")
```

An explicit `theme` argument always takes priority; with neither set, updoc uses
`"auto"`.

Try each theme on the demo popup at the bottom of this page (toggle the site's
light/dark switch in the navbar to compare `"auto"` and `"inverse"`):

<div class="updoc-demo-controls" data-updoc-demo="themes" role="group" aria-label="Preview popup theme">
<button type="button" class="updoc-demo-btn" data-updoc-demo-theme="auto" aria-pressed="true">Auto</button>
<button type="button" class="updoc-demo-btn" data-updoc-demo-theme="inverse" aria-pressed="false">Inverse</button>
<button type="button" class="updoc-demo-btn" data-updoc-demo-theme="light" aria-pressed="false">Light</button>
<button type="button" class="updoc-demo-btn" data-updoc-demo-theme="dark" aria-pressed="false">Dark</button>
</div>

## Other options

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `pkg = "path/to/package"` | Preview another package (any folder or file inside it works); defaults to `"."` |
| `browse = FALSE` | Start the server without opening a browser tab |
| `port = 4567` | Request a specific local port (`0` picks any free port); defaults to `4321` |
| `quiet = TRUE` | Hide detailed pkgdown output while keeping progress, warnings, and errors |

If your requested port is already in use (or you pass `port = 0`), updoc picks
a free local port and prints the URL it chose. The preview server only listens
locally on `127.0.0.1`.

## Automation and AI agents

updoc works cleanly from scripts, CI jobs, and AI coding agents without needing
an interactive R session or browser window.

### One-shot checks

Use [`check()`](../reference/check.html) to verify a package's site in a
temporary copy without touching `man/`, `README.md`, or `docs/`:

```sh
Rscript -e 'updoc::check(format = "json")'
```

It prints one JSON object to standard output (`ok`, `package_root`, `duration`,
`warnings`, `error`, and `build_log`) and exits with a non-zero status on
failure. Pass `error = FALSE` if you want to inspect the JSON result without an
error exit.

### Driving a live preview over HTTP

If an agent or tool keeps a preview server running in the background (use
`port = 0` to avoid collisions across parallel runs):

```sh
Rscript -e 'updoc::serve(port = 0, browse = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)'
```

The preview server exposes three local control endpoints on `127.0.0.1`:

- `GET /__updoc__/status` returns the current build status as JSON, including
  `phase` (`"ready"`, `"building"`, `"error"`), `url`, `rebuild_count`,
  `last_success`, `changed`, `warnings`, `error`, and `build_log`.
- `GET /__updoc__/status?wait=1&timeout=60` checks for any newly saved edits,
  waits until the build settles (or `timeout` seconds pass, up to 300), and
  returns the settled JSON status. Add `&after=<rebuild_count>` to wait for a
  newer build.
- `GET /__updoc__/log` returns the full unfiltered text of the latest build log
  (or `404` before the first build starts).
- `POST /__updoc__/rebuild` (with header `X-Updoc-Request: rebuild`) triggers a
  rebuild; add `?full=true` to force a full site rebuild.

In an R script holding a preview handle, `site$wait(timeout = 60)` provides the
same wait-until-settled behavior directly.

### Bundled agent skill

updoc ships a ready-to-use `SKILL.md` for AI agents inside the installed
package:

```r
system.file("skills", "updoc", "SKILL.md", package = "updoc")
```

See the [`serve()` reference](../reference/serve.html) for the full list of
arguments and defaults.
